# Lab 1.7: Saved Queries, Files & Folders

## What We Are Going to Do
Save a query, see its version history, organise it in a folder, and share it with a colleague.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Save a query.** Open a new query tab and paste:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT state, COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS unique_names
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
GROUP BY state
ORDER BY unique_names DESC;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Click **Save → Save query**. Name it `unique_names_by_state` and pick a region for code assets (for example `us-central1`).

2. **[Console] Create versions.** Change `ORDER BY unique_names DESC` to `ORDER BY state` and save again. Open the query's **Version history** and compare the two versions.

3. **[Console] Organise in folders.** In the Explorer, open the **Files** pane. Create a folder `Module 01` in your personal area and move the saved query into it.

4. **[Console] Share.** Click **Share** on the saved query. Add a colleague with the **Code Viewer** role, so they can open and run it but not change it.

5. **[CLI] See where code assets live.** Saved queries are stored as Dataform repositories in the region you picked.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable dataform.googleapis.com
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  "https://dataform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/repositories" | head -40</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Saved query | `unique_names_by_state` in the Files pane |
| Versions | Two versions you can compare |
| Sharing | Colleague can view and run, not edit |
| Storage | Code assets backed by Dataform |
